title: The Time Capsule
logline: Michael makes the office fill a time capsule for the Dunder Mifflin of 2050, while Dwight hunts whoever keeps stealing his parking spot.
outline: A: Michael's time capsule legacy; B: Dwight's parking spot stakeout; C: Kevin's secret chili. Order: cold, A, A, B, C, C, A, A, B, A, tag.
theme: What we leave behind, and who we really are when we think nobody will look.
storySoFar: Michael is trying to build a legacy. Dwight is convinced someone is targeting his parking spot. Kevin is secretly entering a chili cook-off.

extras.name: Gary Trundle
extras.title: Owner, Trundle Storage Solutions
extras.voice: A painfully literal storage-unit salesman who answers every question with a pricing tier.

scenes.recap: Jim convinces Dwight his desk has been declared a historic landmark.

beats.caption: tapes a tiny brass plaque to Dwight's desk

beats.text: "Historic Landmark. Do Not Alter." Jim. What is this.
The Scranton Historical Society came by. Your desk is protected now. You can't touch it.
That's absurd. I need my stapler.
I wouldn't. That's a federal offense.

lines: I respect history. I come from history.
So I will be working standing up. On the floor. For as long as it takes.

beats.caption: types on a laptop balanced on the copier

beats.text: Pam. In 2050, what will they know about us?
...Hopefully not much?
Exactly. Which is why we are making a time capsule. Conference room. Five minutes.

lines: The pyramids were basically time capsules.
And people still talk about the pharaohs. Nobody talks about the guy who stacked the rocks.
I want to be the pharaoh.

scenes.recap: Michael gathers everyone and reveals the capsule: a hollowed-out water cooler jug.

beats.text: Everyone will put one item in here that represents who they truly are.
Michael, that's the water cooler jug.
It WAS the water cooler jug. Now it is a vessel.
Is this mandatory?
History is mandatory, Stanley.
Oh my God, can I put in my vision board? It has Ryan on it but I can cut him out.
The Party Planning Committee will be overseeing all submissions. Nothing tacky.
I cannot participate. My desk is a protected landmark and my belongings are inside it.
That... is the coolest thing that has ever happened in this office.

lines: In 2050 someone will open that jug.
And they will learn that we ran out of water for three weeks.

scenes.recap: Dwight finds a stranger's minivan in his parking spot again and stakes it out.

beats.text: Third time this week. Same minivan. Same smug little stick-figure family.

beats.caption: presses his face against the minivan window

beats.text: Sir, step away from the vehicle.
I am a volunteer sheriff's deputy. This vehicle is a suspect.
It's a Honda.

lines: Whoever is taking my spot is sending a message.
And I will send one back. In Morse code. With my headlights. All night.

scenes.recap: Oscar catches Kevin 'preparing' his time capsule item: a sealed container of chili.

beats.caption: tastes from a giant tub of chili

beats.text: Kevin. Please tell me that's not going in the time capsule.
It represents who I truly am.
It will be a biohazard by Tuesday.
Then it will be a biohazard of love.

scenes.recap: Jim and Pam plan their own secret capsule entry.

beats.text: What are you putting in?
A drawing of the office. Everyone in it. Even Toby.
Bold choice, including Toby. Michael might not let it in.
I drew him really small. Behind a plant.

lines: Someone in 2050 is going to look at that drawing and think we were friends.
Which... I guess we kind of are.

scenes.recap: Michael asks Darryl to forklift the capsule into the ground; Darryl introduces Gary, who sells storage.

beats.text: Darryl. My man. I need a forklift and a hole. A deep hole.
We're on the second floor of a business park, Mike. There's no ground.
Gary Trundle, Trundle Storage. Climate-controlled units start at forty-nine ninety-nine.
Can it last until 2050?
That's the Platinum tier.
Sold!

lines: Gary was here to pick up a pallet of copy paper.
Now he has a client for twenty-six years. I respect the hustle.

scenes.recap: Angela rejects capsule submissions; Andy's a cappella recording is vetoed.

beats.text: Andy. A cassette of your college a cappella group is not a time capsule item. It's a punishment.
Here Comes Treble is timeless, Angela. Literally. It's in the name. Sort of.

beats.caption: begins a one-man arrangement of 'Rockin' Robin'

beats.text: I'm putting in my divorce papers. Both sets.
Rejected.
I've already put mine in. Don't open it before 2050. Or ever.

lines: Future generations deserve to know that some of us had standards.

scenes.recap: Dwight's stakeout reveals the minivan belongs to Toby.

beats.text: Dwight, it's been four hours.
Shh. The owner always returns to the scene.
TOBY.
Oh. Hi. My spot's been taken by a storage truck all week.

lines: So the storage guy took Toby's spot. Toby took Dwight's spot.
And Dwight's desk is a historic landmark. Honestly, it's been a big week for real estate.

scenes.recap: The capsule is sealed; Michael finds Pam's drawing and sees Toby in it.

beats.text: Final submissions. Pam, what do we have?
It's all of us. The whole office.
Is that... Toby? Behind the plant?
You drew me? Pam, that's really—
No. No no no. Toby does not get to be immortal.
It's a family portrait, Michael. Families have... Tobys.
Fine. But in 2050 I want it known that I was against it.

lines: A legacy is like a family. You don't get to pick who's in it.
But you do get to pick who's behind the plant.

scenes.recap: Michael visits the capsule in its storage unit after one day.

beats.text: I just want to check on it.
Sir, you sealed it yesterday.
And it smells like chili. Why does it smell like chili, Gary?
Odor management is the Titanium tier.

stateChanges.text: Dwight's desk is a 'historic landmark' (Jim's plaque) and he refuses to touch it
Michael is paying Gary Trundle for a Platinum-tier storage unit until 2050; the capsule smells of Kevin's chili
